<a id="summary"></a>

## Summary

The sidecar (s02, plan 228) holds the token and knows the account, endpoint, quota and served models; the daemon never does (d-2). This plan makes the daemon ask it at every Copilot spawn and wire the seat to it only on `ready` (d-6), record proxied or plain on the seat, and watch it every 30 s so primes hear once per change (d-7). Built against the c-status-route contract with the daemon's own struct and a stub server; rebased on s02 before the PR, whose live proof uses s02's real sidecar on a test port.

<a id="goals"></a>

## Goals

- A Copilot seat on a Claude model launches proxied only when the sidecar says ready and serves its base id; every other case launches plain with a reason and a fix (req-04, req-05, req-13).
- Operators and primes can see which seats are proxied, and primes hear once per proxy state change, never repeats (req-09).
- OMP, Claude, Codex and Pi seats are untouched; the daemon adds no process launch (req-12, k-4, k-5).

<a id="non-goals"></a>

## Non-goals

- The sidecar itself, its config file, its LaunchAgent and `pij-rs cache-proxy` verbs (s02, plan 228).
- Holding, reading or passing any token: the daemon reads only the status route.
- Live-fleet receipts for every matrix row (s04).
- Moving already-running seats onto the proxy: they stay plain until revived.

| ac-0001 | Gate and env (req-04, req-05, req-12, req-13). For a Copilot spawn (spawn and revive, both through launch_seat_locked) the seat runs plain when: `--no-cache-proxy` was given (new flag on `pij-rs spawn`, `no_cache_proxy` on SpawnRequest); no `--model` was given (the gate cannot tell the model is Claude); the model is not a Claude id (`claude-` prefix); the status route is unreachable or times out after 1 s (reason "proxy not listening"); the status says anything but `ready` (the status's own reason and fix, so quota exhaustion carries its reset date and machine-wide `off` reads as off); or the base id (model with a trailing `-1m` stripped) is not in the status `models` (reason "model not served by Copilot API"). Otherwise the launch command gains `COPILOT_PROVIDER_TYPE=anthropic`, `COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL=&lt;proxy url&gt;`, `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MODEL_ID=&lt;base id&gt;` and `COPILOT_PROVIDER_MAX_PROMPT_TOKENS=&lt;max_prompt_tokens&gt;`. Omp, Claude, Codex and Pi spawns make no status GET and get no provider env. The proxy URL is `http://127.0.0.1:7471`, overridden only by `PIJ_CACHE_PROXY_URL` read once at daemon start (tests). | [ ] unchecked | — | — | [bp-0001](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | — |
| ac-0002 | Seat state and receipt (req-04, req-09). A Copilot seat with no recorded field (launched before this) reads as plain with the reason "launched before the cache proxy". Non-Copilot seats carry none. A revive re-runs the gate; a seat spawned with `--no-cache-proxy` stays opted out on revive. | [ ] unchecked | — | — | [bp-0002](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | — |

| ac-0004 | Watch and notices (req-08, req-09). The daemon reads the status route every 30 s (one loopback GET, no launch). The first reading after daemon start is the baseline: silent when it is `ready`, or when no live Copilot seat is recorded proxied; when it is not ready and live proxied seats exist, it sends the one notice, so a sidecar that died while the daemon was down is still reported (pm-004 ruling). Each later change of `state`, including becoming unreachable and coming back, sends exactly one notice to each distinct live prime (every project's prime and the machine's designated prime, once each), naming the old and new state, the reason, the fix and the live proxied seats; an unchanged state sends nothing, however long it lasts. `/health` gains `cache_proxy`: the URL, whether it answered, the last status (with counters), when it was read, and the live Copilot seats split into proxied and plain, so `pij-rs --json ping` shows it. | [ ] unchecked | — | — | [bp-0004](assets/backpressure.dd.md#rows) | — |

<a id="research-context"></a>

## Research Context

Code map (origin/main 84ef0774): launch_seat_locked (crates/daemon/src/http/mod.rs ~1363) builds SpawnPlanInput then the descriptor and persists it under the spawn lock; build_spawn_plan (crates/harnesses/src/spawn.rs) emits `env PIJ_SESSION_ID=… PIJ_SPAWN_ID=… <harness> …`, so provider env joins that prefix; SeatDescriptor (crates/core/src/model.rs) is stored as normalized seats columns (crates/store/src/registry.rs upsert_seat, row_to_descriptor), so a new field needs a column; registration mutates the existing descriptor (registration.rs ~1089), so the field survives binding. notify_prime (crates/daemon/src/http/routes.rs) resolves one project's prime (own, else machine designated) and holds one FYI; the watch generalises that resolution to every distinct live prime. Periodic work uses lifecycle::TickLoop (crates/daemon/src/lifecycle.rs); reqwest is already a daemon dependency. Copilot's own `/restart` re-execs in place [INFERENCE: keeps its env], so the notice's fix names `pij-rs revive`, which re-runs the gate; row 7's live proof checks which one comes up plain.

<a id="risks"></a>

## Risks

| risk | likelihood | impact | mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Copilot `/restart` keeps the provider env, so a seat on a dead proxy stays broken after it. | Medium | Medium | The notice's fix names `pij-rs revive &lt;seat&gt;` (re-runs the gate); row 7 proves which path comes up plain and the result goes to pm-004. |
| The 1 s status GET runs under the spawn lock and delays other spawns when the sidecar hangs. | Low | Low | Hard 1 s timeout, Copilot spawns only; any failure is plain. |
| Field names drift from s02's status route. | Medium | Medium | Own struct with serde defaults for every field except `state`; rebase on s02 and prove against its real sidecar before the PR. |
| A notice per change floods primes if the sidecar flaps. | Low | Low | One per change is the contract (row 21); the 30 s poll bounds the rate at 2 a minute; reported if seen. |

<a id="execution-guardrails"></a>

## Execution Guardrails

- Builds only via `PIJ_SHARED_TARGET=/Users/jordanknight/pi-hacking/target-ws004 just shared-build -- <cargo args>`, -p scoped, one per change; stop and tell pm-004 on a disk-floor refusal.
- Tests use scratch repos and a private daemon (own state dir and port); never the prod daemon, never the live governance branch; never install a LaunchAgent.
- Never read credential files or print a token; the daemon reads only the status route.
- No `git add -A`, no `--no-verify`, no `npm install`, no pushing refs/notes/*; trailers Pij-Seat, Pij-Prime: pij-far-jackal, Pij-Plan: 229-cache-proxy-gate.
- After the PR is out for verdicts, push nothing unless a verdict asks, and tell pm-004 first.
